# [R6 — Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/openproblem_r6.py`: what the data held here can and cannot show about the hypothesis. Each marked statement links to what it rests on.*

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-CLASS">**Missing: experiment, constructive.** [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate")'s discriminator is a *rate* against a *ratio* - sediment Fe:S and Fe:P against phosphate release rate - and its causal clause is comparative: marine sediment releases more phosphate under anoxia *because of the sulphate*. A field record varies sulphate only together with salinity, organic loading, iron supply and temperature, so the contrast has to be built, in a core incubation.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-CLASS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## No water-column observable can reach it, and this should be said plainly

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-PANEL">The archive's finest routine observable near the bed is a monthly median per station: `stations_series.json` holds [679,422](../SOURCES.md#F-b61d7944ec) station-months at [1,415](../SOURCES.md#F-fff0060a3d) stations over [564](../SOURCES.md#F-008df4b99b) months from [1980](../SOURCES.md#F-44433af5f2), near-bed oxygen on [76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf) of them.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-PANEL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-SCALE">[R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate") lives at the sulphide front, which the national sediment reports place millimetres to centimetres below the sediment surface; a station-month median of bottom-water oxygen is far coarser in space and time, and the wrong quantity besides: oxygen is [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate")'s *precondition*, not its consequence.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-SCALE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-CONFOUND">A correlation between bed oxygen and water-column phosphate is equally predicted by [A7](../openproblems/A7.md "Sediment nutrient regeneration"), [R2](../HYPOTHESES.md "Priming of the old sediment pool by fresh carbon"), [R5](../HYPOTHESES.md "The terminal electron acceptor cascade, and why salt changes it") and plain mineralisation. **Unscoreable here, not refuted.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-CONFOUND "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-H2S">**The `Dihydrogensulfid` series, checked rather than assumed.** The CTD extract's `Dihydrogensulfid` has [2,601](../SOURCES.md#F-8d6ff9b8d2) records at [4](../SOURCES.md#F-d29c2aa9f6) stations, [2,598](../SOURCES.md#F-906d8ca940) of them from station `93610032` in Mariager Fjord.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-H2S "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-H2SUSE">One silled fjord whose inner basin exchanges little water: usable for the <span class="chem" data-chem="H2S" title="hydrogen sulphide">H₂S</span> climatology of Mariager Fjord's bottom water and nothing comparative.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-H2SUSE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-ENDPOINT">It is also the wrong side of the mechanism: **free sulphide in the water column is what remains after the sediment's iron buffer is spent**, a detector of the endpoint, not of the process.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-ENDPOINT "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-KEMIH2S">The held water-chemistry extract carries sulphide from bottles under two names, `Dihydrogensulfid` on [1,188](../SOURCES.md#F-6b152a6536) records and `Svovlbrinte (sulfid)` on [621](../SOURCES.md#F-9afe347e71): a separate production path, measuring the same endpoint.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-KEMIH2S "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What exists

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-SR323">**DCE's SR323**, *Sammenhænge i det marine miljø* (`dce2.au.dk/pub/SR323.pdf`), analyses the national sediment programme: loss on ignition, total N, total P and iron-bound P in the top [10](../SOURCES.md#F-f71f48c3be) cm at [12](../SOURCES.md#F-20578fffc4) stations measured both in 1999–2003 and in 2017–2018, in [7](../SOURCES.md#F-9fe7a3561b) Danish fjord areas, the Sydfynske Øhav and northern Øresund; the sulphide front and buffer capacity in [16](../SOURCES.md#F-491428cc45) areas, spring and autumn; and, in open waters from 2005 to 2015, sulphide at [16](../SOURCES.md#F-3918efedcf) of [20](../SOURCES.md#F-3918efedcf) stations.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-SR323 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-TA14">**NOVA teknisk anvisning `kap. 14`** (1998), the national method: the sulphide front by silver plate (`§14.7.1.1`), the sulphide buffer capacity (`§14.7.1.2`), oxidised iron in the buffer zone (`§14.7.1.3`), iron-bound phosphorus (`§14.6.1.1`), and the fluxes of oxygen and nutrients, ortho-phosphate among them, between incubated cores and the water above them (`§14.8`).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-TA14 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

This project's reading of it is a note in the source register, from an analysis not stored as a script, and the note does not say whether iron, sulphur and phosphorus were measured on the same samples.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-DOME "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-PG997075">**PANGAEA `997075`**: Kiel Bight sediment cores collected in February 2025 and incubated under controlled oxygen cycles, with sequential iron extraction, total sulphur, hydrogen sulphide, sulphate, ammonium, alkalinity and sulphate reduction rates by radiotracer; from GEOMAR, a production path separate from Danish monitoring.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-PG997075 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-PG997075-NOP">Its record lists no phosphorus measurement.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-PG997075-NOP "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What the national method measured

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-METHOD">The 1998 method specifies the buffer capacity as a titration of the sulphide-free surface sediment with <span class="chem" data-chem="H2S" title="hydrogen sulphide">H₂S</span>, reported as µmol of <span class="chem" data-chem="H2S" title="hydrogen sulphide">H₂S</span> consumed per cm², and measures oxidised iron in the same zone so the two can be related: a *functional assay of the reactive iron pool* [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate") turns on.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-METHOD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-RESULTS">DCE's SR323 reports from it, as means over the areas: the front rose from [51](../SOURCES.md#F-fae586dd58) mm below the surface in spring to [25](../SOURCES.md#F-fae586dd58) mm in autumn, and the buffer capacity fell from [29](../SOURCES.md#F-7ffa2a296c) to [15](../SOURCES.md#F-7ffa2a296c) µmol cm⁻²; its figure's bars give the spread over 1998–2003. Oxidised iron in the top [1.5](../SOURCES.md#F-2bed4cf5ba) cm ranged from [2](../SOURCES.md#F-2bed4cf5ba) to [2,741](../SOURCES.md#F-2bed4cf5ba) µmol, with geometric means of [9.3](../SOURCES.md#F-b88094c201) in spring and [2.0](../SOURCES.md#F-b88094c201) in autumn once Limfjorden and Ringkøbing Fjord are set aside.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-RESULTS "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-CONSUMED">The report reads the two seasonal changes as of the same order - iron consumed as the sulphide front advances, in Danish sediment, seasonally - while noting that other substances than oxidised iron add to the buffer capacity and that the iron was measured only near the surface.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-CONSUMED "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-CENSOR">**Censoring.** Where the oxidised zone is deep, the added sediment can consume all the <span class="chem" data-chem="H2S" title="hydrogen sulphide">H₂S</span> added (≈ [100](../SOURCES.md#F-3b91ef5350) µmol), and the method then reports the buffer capacity as `>x µmol cm-2`: right-censored precisely at the high-iron stations [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate") cares most about.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-CENSOR "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Why experiment, and the null it must be run against

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-STATE">Running the 1998 assay would give iron and sulphur as *state variables* - worth doing, and only a measurement problem. It still would not test [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate"), which asserts a **causal dependence of phosphate release on sulphate**, and the field never varies sulphate alone.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-STATE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-NULL">The naive null - "anoxic sediment releases no more phosphate than oxic sediment" - is wrong, and would hand [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate") a win it has not earned: under anoxia phosphate is released by the breakdown of organic matter, and iron-reducing bacteria free iron-bound phosphate, whether or not sulphide forms.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-NULL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-NULL2">The constraint an incubation imposes is *same sediment, same anoxia, sulphate varied*. So the null is **equality of phosphate release per unit mineralisation across sulphate levels** - flux(<span class="chem" data-chem="PO4 3-" title="phosphate">PO₄³⁻</span>) normalised to concurrent flux(DIC) or <span class="chem" data-chem="NH4+" title="ammonium">NH₄⁺</span> from the same core, sulphate the only manipulated term. Under `H0` that ratio is flat in sulphate; [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate") predicts it rises and saturates where reactive iron is exhausted. A design without a sulphate-free *anoxic* arm cannot reject anything, however many replicates it has.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-NULL2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Smallest unblocking thing

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-S1">**Run the 1998 assay at [20](../SOURCES.md#F-6d6b903f5d) existing `Bundfauna` stations, one spring and one autumn.** Silver-plate front, buffer capacity, oxidised iron, beside the iron-adsorbed phosphorus `Sedimentkemi` already carries. Report the censoring threshold with every `>` value. Cost: a protocol that already exists in Danish, a syringe and a photometer.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-S1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-S2">**The incubation.** One Danish sediment, homogenised, split across a sulphate dose series from [1](../SOURCES.md#F-7b5cb6b6c8) to [28](../SOURCES.md#F-989bdfa634) mM at fixed ionic strength by NaCl substitution, so *sulphate* is the treatment. Track <span class="chem" data-chem="PO4 3-" title="phosphate">PO₄³⁻</span>, DIC/<span class="chem" data-chem="NH4+" title="ammonium">NH₄⁺</span>, <span class="chem" data-chem="H2S" title="hydrogen sulphide">H₂S</span> and sulphate reduction rate in the overlying water; sequential iron (ascorbate/dithionite) and sulphur (AVS/CRS) on the cores at the end.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-S2 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-S2B">PANGAEA `997075` makes sulphate, sulphide, ammonium, sulphate-reduction and sequential-iron measurements together on Kiel Bight sediment in 2025; it names no phosphorus measurement, and phosphorus is the whole of [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate").</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-S2B "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-S3">**Reclassification test, stated in advance.** If the NOVA-era rows (front, buffer, oxidised iron, 1998–2003) are recoverable from the former county archives at ≥[10](../SOURCES.md#F-d82c05b0fc) stations with ≥[4](../SOURCES.md#F-9c592adf52) paired seasons *and* a co-located iron-adsorbed phosphorus value, [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate")'s **state** half becomes **armchair** and this page is half wrong. The **rate** half stays experimental regardless.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-S3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What it would and would not license

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-R6-LICENSE">A successful incubation licenses one narrow thing: *in this sediment, sulphate availability changes phosphate release per unit mineralisation by this factor*. It would **not** license a Danish phosphorus budget, a water-body allocation, or a claim about the Baltic feedback - one sediment is one sediment, and [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate")'s unit is depositional history, not a map. Nor the freshwater comparison [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate") makes in words: that needs the same dose series on lake sediment, and Danish lake and marine sediments differ in much more than sulphate. The honest limit is that it tests the *step* - sulphide strips iron, iron was holding phosphate - not the *system claim* that this is what makes the marine case worse.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-R6-LICENSE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
